dossiers.label: The myth of the reversed cosmos
dossiers.about: Sometimes the god himself guides the world round; then he lets go of the tiller and it turns back of itself the opposite way. In the age of Cronus the god shepherded mankind and men were born from the earth and grew younger; in our age the world runs by itself and forgets. The divine shepherd is not our king.

passage.start_quote: συχνῷ γὰρ μέρει δεῖ μεγάλου μύθου προσχρήσασθαι
passage.end_quote: καὶ τὸ μὲν δὴ τοῦ μύθου τέλος ἐχέτω

parts.quote: τὸ γὰρ πᾶν τόδε τοτὲ μὲν αὐτὸς ὁ θεὸς συμποδηγεῖ πορευόμενον καὶ συγκυκλεῖ, τοτὲ δὲ ἀνῆκεν

parts.quote: τοῦ παντὸς ὁ μὲν κυβερνήτης, οἷον πηδαλίων οἴακος ἀφέμενος

echoes.why: The Laws tells again of life under Cronus, when daimons ruled men.
The Timaeus' maker, who rejoiced at the moving world.

related.why: The pilot and the helm again, here of the whole world.
After the myth the Stranger turns to a small model, weaving.

web.title: Statesman (dialogue)
web.quote: a myth similar to the myth of ages

dossiers.label: Statesmanship as weaving
dossiers.about: The small model for the king: weaving woollen cloth, divided from its neighbouring arts. The statesman's art at last rules the others and weaves the city together, binding the brave and the moderate characters, warp and woof, into one fabric of concord and friendship.

passage.end_quote: περιήλθομεν ἐν κύκλῳ πάμπολλα διοριζόμενοι μάτην

parts.label: Interweaving of warp and woof
parts.quote: πλεκτικὴν εἶναι κρόκης καὶ στήμονος ὑφαντικήν

echoes.why: The art that rules the others and weaves everything together rightly is statesmanship.

echoes.quote: τοῦτο δὴ τέλος ὑφάσματος εὐθυπλοκίᾳ συμπλακὲν
echoes.why: The end of the work: the brave and the moderate woven into one fabric.

related.why: The Sophist's small model, chosen the same way.
